answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps agents into a trust graph structured as an clustered grove. Multi-agent auditing audits interactions through an analytical prism, cross-validating sparse topological cut verifications across clusters. When fake identities collude to fabricate consensus, honest verifiers detect min-cut bottlenecks, slashing deposited stakes. Reaching the summit of influence imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(N^2)$.
